age.evidence: Female Sprague-Dawley rats (N = 96) aged 6 weeks ... 16-week recovery period before drug administration

dosing.evidence: Rats received intraperitoneal injections of either psilocybin (dissolved in saline and given at a dose of 1 mg/kg and a volume of 1 mg/ml)

handling.evidence: After an initial period of habituation on arrival to the facility, animals were handled for 1 week before experimental procedures began.

group_housing.evidence: The rats were housed in groups of 4

day_night_flipped.evidence: maintained on a 12-h light-dark cycle (direction of cycle not specified)

enrichment_housing.evidence: Paper describes housing in groups of 4 and bedding changes but does not mention enrichment items.

assays.assay_description: Rats placed individually in a bedded cage identical to home cage immediately after psilocybin or saline injection; head-twitches counted for 15 min. Used to confirm 5-HT2A engagement.

application_type.evidence: Rats received intraperitoneal injections of either psilocybin

setup_habituation.evidence: rats were placed individually into a bedded cage identical to their home-cage immediately after psilocybin or saline treatment

setup_restrain.evidence: placed individually into a bedded cage

food_restriction.evidence: No food was placed in the observation cage during the 15 min recording

water_restriction.evidence: No water was placed in the observation cage during the 15 min recording

time_to_assay.evidence: placed individually into a bedded cage... immediately after psilocybin or saline treatment

sample_size.evidence: we scored head-twitching behavior in a randomly selected subset of rats (8 per group)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg) markedly increased head twitches in both sham and mTBI+NFS rats; the response was abolished by M100907 pre-treatment, confirming 5-HT2A receptor mediation.
outcomes.statistics: Kruskal-Wallis H = 52.850, p < 0.001; saline/saline vs saline/psilocybin: U = 3.508, p < 0.001 (sham); U = 3.470, p < 0.001 (mTBI+NFS); saline/psilocybin vs M100907/psilocybin: U = 3.486, p < 0.001
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin increased head twitching in both sham (saline/saline vs saline/psilocybin: U = 3.508, p < 0.001) and mTBI+NFS rats... Psilocybin's effects were abolished by M100907

B1_num_measures.evidence: the number of head-twitches was recorded

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric

E1_environment_type.evidence: bedded cage identical to their home-cage

E8_food_water.evidence: no food/water in observation cage during 15 min recording

D1_continuity.evidence: recorded for a duration of 15 min

D2_session_duration.evidence: recorded for a duration of 15 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: immediately after psilocybin or saline treatment

assays.assay_description: '+'-shaped maze with two open and two enclosed arms (50×10 cm), elevated above ground. Rats placed in centre and explored for 5 min. Time in each arm and arm entries recorded via TopScan.

food_restriction.evidence: no food in EPM during test

water_restriction.evidence: no water in EPM during test

time_to_assay.evidence: Twenty-four hours after treatment, rats were tested in the elevated-plus maze

sample_size.evidence: A priori power analysis revealed that a sample size of 12 rats per group was sufficient

outcomes.summary: Injured rats showed more open-arm entries (impulsivity-like). Psilocybin recovered open-arm time and entries toward sham levels (~46% and 92% recovery); effect partially blocked by M100907.
outcomes.statistics: Open arm time: F(1,88)=4.800, p=0.031; Open arm entries injury × psilocybin interaction: F(1,88)=5.070, p=0.027 (mTBI+NFS saline/saline vs sham saline/saline p=0.046)
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin treatment recovered open arm time in injured rats to control levels by 46%... Psilocybin reversed the injury-induced increase in open arm entries to control levels by 92%.

B1_num_measures.evidence: time spent in each arm and the number of entries into each arm

E2_shelter.evidence: closed arms not scored as shelter per rubric

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM scored as single space per rubric

assays.assay_description: Circular open-field arena (100 cm diameter), well-lit. Rats placed in centre and monitored for 5 min. Time in centre, centre entries, distance travelled, velocity, latency recorded via TopScan.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were placed in the center... exploratory behavior was monitored

food_restriction.evidence: no food in OFT during test

water_restriction.evidence: no water in OFT during test

time_to_assay.evidence: The open field test was performed 2-days post-treatment

sample_size.evidence: A priori power analysis revealed that a sample size of 12 rats per group was sufficient

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin-treated rats spent less time in the centre overall, but no significant post-hoc group differences. No effects on entries, distance, velocity, or latency.
outcomes.statistics: F(1,88)=4.223, p=0.043 (main effect of psilocybin on centre time)
outcomes.evidence: rats treated with psilocybin spent a reduced amount of time in the centre of the arena [F(1, 88) = 4.223, p = 0.043], there were no significant post-hoc group differences

B1_num_measures.evidence: time in centre, entries into centre, distance travelled, velocity, latency to enter centre

assays.assay_description: Y-shaped arena. Sample phase: 10 min with 2 arms accessible. 1 h later, test phase: 5 min with all 3 arms accessible. Time in each arm, entries, and spontaneous alternation % recorded via TopScan.

time_to_assay.evidence: Three days after treatment, cognitive function was evaluated by re-assessing spatial memory using the Y-maze test

sample_size.evidence: A priori power analysis revealed that a sample size of 12 rats per group was sufficient

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin significantly increased time spent in the novel arm and modulated spontaneous alternation. In injured rats, psilocybin's pro-cognitive effect on novel arm time was blocked by M100907 (96%).
outcomes.statistics: Novel arm time: F(1,88)=8.812, p=0.026; M100907 × psilocybin interaction F(1,88)=8.398, p=0.005; sham saline/psilocybin vs sham saline/saline p=0.015; spontaneous alternation F(1,88)=4.853, p=0.030
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin treatment significantly increased the time spent in the novel arm of the Y-maze [F(1, 88) = 8.812, p = 0.026]

B1_num_measures.evidence: time spent in each arm, number of entries, spontaneous alternation %

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: alternation % is a composite, not transition analysis

D1_continuity.evidence: 10 min sample phase + 5 min test phase 1 h later

D3_recording_days.evidence: both phases on same day, 3 days post-treatment

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug baseline (acute Y-maze pre-injury is a separate paradigm)

assays.assay_description: Rotating barrel divided into four lanes. After habituation at 4 rpm and ramp trials, 3 test trials with speed increasing from 4 to 40 rpm over 5 min. Latency to fall recorded by sensor.

setup_habituation.evidence: rats were habituated to remain on the rotarod at a constant speed of 4 rotations per minute (rpm) for 2 min

time_to_assay.evidence: The rotarod test was conducted 4 days after treatment

sample_size.evidence: A priori power analysis revealed that a sample size of 12 rats per group was sufficient

outcomes.summary: Injured rats fell from the rotarod quicker than sham rats; psilocybin recovered fall latency in injured rats by 73%, though no significant post-hoc group differences.
outcomes.statistics: F(1,88)=8.279, p=0.005 (injury effect on fall latency)
outcomes.evidence: Injured rats fell from the rotarod quicker than sham rats... Psilocybin recovered fall latency in injured rats by 73%.

D1_continuity.evidence: 3 consecutive test trials on one day

assays.assay_description: Black circular pool (163 cm diameter) with hidden platform; 4 spatial cues. Acquisition day: 10 trials to find platform (max 60 s). Reversal day (24 h later): platform moved to opposite quadrant, 10 trials. Latency to find platform measured.

water_restriction.evidence: no drinking water access during trial

time_to_assay.evidence: water maze test over two consecutive days, 5- and 6-days post-treatment

sample_size.evidence: A priori power analysis revealed that a sample size of 12 rats per group was sufficient

outcomes.summary: All groups learned the platform location across blocks. In the reversal phase, mTBI+NFS rats had longer platform search times in multiple blocks; psilocybin-treated injured rats found the platform quicker in block 4 than saline-treated injured rats.
outcomes.statistics: Reversal Friedman block 1-5: 217.264, p<0.001; Kruskal-Wallis block 2: H=18.385, p=0.010; block 3: H=15.884, p=0.026; block 4: H=19.627, p=0.006; block 5: H=18.309, p=0.011; mTBI+NFS saline/psilocybin vs saline/saline block 4: U=2.483, p=0.012
outcomes.evidence: mTBI+NFS rats that were treated with saline/psilocybin found the platform quicker in block 4 than mTBI+NFS rats treated with saline/saline (U = 2.483, p = 0.012).

B1_num_measures.evidence: amount of time it took to find the platform

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: 10 trials grouped into 5 blocks (2 trials per block)

E2_shelter.evidence: no shelter (platform doesn't count as refuge)

D2_session_duration.evidence: 10 trials per day with up to 60 s per trial plus 15 s on platform between trials

assays.assay_description: Glass cylinder (24 cm diameter, 40 cm high) with water at 23-25°C, 30 cm depth. Day 1: 10 min pre-test. Day 2 (24 h later): 5 min test recorded; immobility, swimming, climbing/struggling manually scored.

setup_habituation.evidence: This session served to teach the rats of the inescapable nature of the cylinder

setup_restrain.evidence: FST cylinder (per rubric, FST is considered restraint)

time_to_assay.evidence: First, 7-days post-treatment... Twenty-four hours later, the rats were reintroduced

sample_size.evidence: A priori power analysis revealed that a sample size of 12 rats per group was sufficient

outcomes.summary: Significant 3-way interaction (injury × M100907 × psilocybin) on immobility time; psilocybin reduced injury-induced immobility (120% recovery) in absence of M100907, partially blocked by M100907 (67%). No significant post-hoc differences and no effects on swimming/climbing.
outcomes.statistics: F(1,88)=4.099, p=0.046 (injury × M100907 × psilocybin interaction on immobility)
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin recovering immobility time (by 120%) in the absence of M100907, which partially blocked psilocybin's recovery by 67%

B1_num_measures.evidence: time spent swimming, climbing/struggling, and immobile

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility explicitly excluded from ethological

D1_continuity.evidence: 10 min pre-test + 5 min test 24 h later

D4_baseline.evidence: pre-test is post-drug; no pre-drug FST baseline

assays.assay_description: Temperature-controlled plate enclosed by transparent cylinder. After 2 min habituation, hot plate test at 52°C; 1 h later cold plate at 2°C. Latency to first reaction (lick/jump) recorded; max 2 min per trial.

setup_habituation.evidence: rats were habituated to a small circular temperature-controlled plate... for 2 min

setup_restrain.evidence: rat freely placed on plate within enclosure

sample_size.evidence: A priori power analysis revealed that a sample size of 12 rats per group was sufficient

outcomes.summary: Hot plate: no significant group effect, but psilocybin increased latency to react in injured rats (146% recovery, blocked 84% by M100907). Cold plate: mTBI+NFS reduced latency relative to sham, indicating hyperalgesia; psilocybin did not significantly alter cold response.
outcomes.statistics: Cold plate: H=17.845, p=0.013; mTBI+NFS saline/saline vs sham saline/saline U=2.579, p=0.020; mTBI+NFS M100907/saline vs sham M100907/saline U=2.649, p=0.042
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin increased the latency to react in injured rats, scoring a percentage recovery of 146%... injured rats reacted to the cold plate sooner than sham rats (H = 17.845, p = 0.013)

B1_num_measures.evidence: latency on hot plate and on cold plate

D1_continuity.evidence: hot plate then cold plate 1 h later

assays.assay_description: Three-chamber acrylic arena (100×100×50 cm). Three 10-min stages: habituation, social preference (one stimulus rat in mesh cage vs empty), social novelty (familiar vs novel stimulus). Time in chambers and sniff zones measured.

setup_habituation.evidence: The initial stage served as a habituation session, allowing the test rat... to freely explore the arena

time_to_assay.evidence: The social interaction test was employed 10-days post-treatment

sample_size.evidence: A priori power analysis revealed that a sample size of 12 rats per group was sufficient

outcomes.summary: No effects on social preference in trial 2. In trial 3 (social novelty), injury increased novel-rat preference; psilocybin reversed this (91% reversal in absence of M100907, blocked by M100907) without significant post-hoc differences.
outcomes.statistics: Trial 3 novel rat preference injury effect: F(1,88)=10.481, p=0.002
outcomes.evidence: Injury significantly increased novel rat preference in trial 3 [F(1, 88) = 10.481, p = 0.002], although no significant post-hoc differences were detected.

B1_num_measures.evidence: time spent in each chamber, as well as the 'sniff zone' beside the metal cage

B4_ethological.evidence: social investigation/sniffing of conspecific is a natural ethological behaviour

B5_social.evidence: stimulus rat placed in the metal cage... preventing direct physical interaction

E6_spatial.evidence: three equally sized chambers separated by dividing walls

E7_social_context.evidence: stimulus rat placed in metal mesh cage

D1_continuity.evidence: three 10-min stages with cage cleaned between each

assays.assay_description: Rats individually housed for the test with one bottle of water and one bottle of 1% sucrose solution for 24 h (bottle sides switched at 12 h). Sucrose preference calculated as % sucrose intake relative to total fluid intake.

setup_habituation.evidence: given a 24-h habituation period with access to two bottles of 1% sucrose solution

food_restriction.evidence: had access to food and water available ad libitum (home-cage style testing cage)

water_restriction.evidence: one bottle of water and one bottle of 1% sucrose for 24 h

sample_size.evidence: A priori power analysis revealed that a sample size of 12 rats per group was sufficient

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin significantly increased sucrose preference, with a strong injury × psilocybin interaction. mTBI+NFS saline/psilocybin rats had greater sucrose preference than mTBI+NFS saline/saline rats (169% recovery), an effect partially blocked by M100907 (33%).
outcomes.statistics: F(1,88)=12.049, p<0.001 (psilocybin main effect); injury × psilocybin F(1,88)=7.172, p=0.009; mTBI+NFS saline/psilocybin vs mTBI+NFS saline/saline p<0.001
outcomes.evidence: mTBI+NFS saline/psilocybin rats had an increased preference for sucrose compared to mTBI+NFS saline/saline rats (p < 0.001). The 169% recovery by psilocybin was partially blocked by M100907 (33%).

B1_num_measures.evidence: percentage of sucrose solution consumed relative to total fluid intake was calculated (preference score = 1 measure)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: single 24-h summary, sides switched but not analysed over time

B5_social.evidence: each rat separated into own cage

E1_environment_type.evidence: each rat was separated into their own cage

E3_bedding.evidence: home cage with standard bedding (bedding changed weekly in housing)

E7_social_context.evidence: each rat was separated into their own cage

E8_food_water.evidence: given one bottle of water and one bottle of 1% sucrose for 24 h

D4_baseline.evidence: habituation day was not used as a reported baseline measure

judge_notes: Dropped gptoss's placeholder 'Open Field (re-tested for completeness)' assay — it was an explicit duplicate stub.

Excluded the acute pre-treatment Y-maze, beam-walk, neurological/sensorimotor screens, and acute injury severity measures (apnea, toe-pinch latency, self-right) because they were collected BEFORE psilocybin administration (during/immediately after the injury phase, 16 weeks pre-drug), and no psychedelic had been administered at those timepoints.

Resolved candidate disagreements on time_to_assay by using calendar days from injection to test session: OFT (day 2), Y-maze (day 3), rotarod (day 4), water maze (days 5-6), FST (days 7-8), hot/cold plate (day 9), social interaction (day 10), sucrose preference (day 11). Multiple candidates used '24 h' as the time_to_assay for all chronic tests, which was incorrect.
Sucrose preference D1 scored as 'Continuous monitoring' (24 h continuous access in home-cage-style setup) per rubric definition, raising the SPT raw_total to 7.
EPM E6_spatial scored 0 per explicit rubric instruction (EPM arms are open-ended extensions, not distinct compartments).
HTR B4_ethological scored 0 per explicit rubric exclusion (HTR/WDS not ethological).
Three-chamber B4_ethological scored 1 because sniffing of a conspecific is explicitly listed as ethological in the rubric.
FST setup_restrain scored 'yes' per rubric (FST cylinder explicitly listed as restraint).
day_night_flipped set to 'not_reported' (high confidence) because the paper mentions a 12-h light/dark cycle without specifying direction; gptoss's 'no' was an over-inference.
